patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Microsoft Project documents a broader use-case set; VektorOS is narrower/specialist.

General-purpose vs specialist. Choose Microsoft Project only if your buying job matches “Microsoft 365 project / Planner ladder for Gantt, resources and portfolios — Planner Plan ” rather than VektorOS's shape. Choose VektorOS only if your buying job matches “Business and operations software — affiliate partner in project management.” rather than Microsoft Project's shape. Workflow advantage: Microsoft Project leans project-tracking, resource-planning; VektorOS leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Microsoft Project documents a broader use-case set; VektorOS is narrower/specialist.
- Positioning: Microsoft Project is Microsoft 365 project / Planner ladder for Gantt, resources and portfolios — Planner Plan 1 from ~$10/user/mo.; VektorOS is Business and operations software — affiliate partner in project management..
- Company-size focus: Microsoft Project (mid-market, enterprise) vs VektorOS (small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Microsoft Project-leaning project-tracking, resource-planning, timeline-reporting vs VektorOS-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Microsoft Project — SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans; VektorOS — SMB ops platform — limited public pricing transparency.

Limitations — Microsoft Project: SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans; Best value assumes Microsoft 365 standardisation; VektorOS: SMB ops platform — limited public pricing transparency.

Poor-fit cases: Microsoft Project is a poor fit when that limitation bites: SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans · VektorOS is a poor fit when that limitation bites: SMB ops platform — limited public pricing transparency · Avoid Microsoft Project if you actually need VektorOS's motion (Business and operations software — affiliate partner in project management.)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
